theme: Counting Others’ Strength When You’re Nervous
hindi: दुर्योधन द्रोणाचार्य से कहता है: इस सेना में बड़े-बड़े धनुषधारी वीर हैं, जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुन के समान हैं। उनमें युयुधान (सात्यकि), राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं।
english: Duryodhana continues to Drona: “In this army are mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna. Among them are Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the great chariot-warrior.”
deeper: Duryodhana has just asked Drona to look at the Pandava army. Now he begins to name its heroes one by one. On the surface it sounds like a simple report. But notice what he is doing: he is counting the strength of the other side. When we feel unsure inside, our mind often starts counting the strengths of whoever we are about to face.

The names matter too. Yuyudhana (also called Satyaki) was a brave warrior and a close friend of Krishna. Virata was the king who sheltered the Pandavas during their hidden year. Drupada was the father of Draupadi, the Pandavas’ wife. These were not hired soldiers; they were friends and relatives who stood by the Pandavas. The verse quietly shows that the Pandavas were strong because they had loyal friends, not only because of their own skill.

For us, the verse is a gentle mirror. It is good to look honestly at what lies ahead of us. But if we only stare at others’ strengths and forget our own preparation, fear grows. The Gita will slowly teach Arjuna, and us, how to meet a hard moment with a steady mind. This verse shows us how a restless, worried mind behaves before that teaching begins.
background: The Gita begins with the blind king Dhritarashtra asking Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas did on the field of Kurukshetra (1.1). Sanjaya describes how Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava army arranged for battle, went straight to his teacher Drona (1.2).

In the previous verse, Duryodhana pointed to the great Pandava army, arranged by Drupada’s son, who was once Drona’s own student (1.3). Now, in this verse, he begins to list the famous warriors standing in that army.
lessons: Look honestly at what you face
It is wise to know the strengths of a challenge, but do not let it shrink your courage.
Fear often shows up as counting
When we feel nervous, we may keep listing reasons why the other side is strong.
The Pandava army was powerful because loyal friends and family stood with them.
Seeing what others do well is a good habit when it leads to respect and learning, not worry.
Hard moments feel lighter when we have practised and have good people beside us.
examples: Aarav saw the other school’s team practising and began listing how good each player was. His coach said, “Good, you have noticed. Now let’s also remember how well we have practised.”
Meera kept thinking about how smart her classmates were before the Maths Olympiad. She felt calmer when she opened her notebook and saw how many problems she had already solved.
When Rohan’s family moved to a new city, his old friends called him every week. He realised that having people who stand by you is a kind of strength that no marks can measure.
Divya’s relay team was nervous about a faster team. They stopped comparing and practised their baton passing again and again. Teamwork was their biggest strength.
Kabir talked non-stop about how tough his rivals were before the quiz. His mother smiled and said, “When we are nervous, we talk a lot. Take a deep breath first.”
Sana saw how beautifully her friend Tara drew. Instead of feeling small, she asked Tara for tips and improved her own drawing.
Ishaan checked the draw sheet and saw strong names in his group. His father said, “It is fine to know who you will play. Now go and play your best game.”
Before her dance show, Lakshmi thanked her teacher, her mother who stitched the costume, and her friends who rehearsed with her. She felt that many people were standing behind her.

story.title: The Pigeons and the Net
paras: In an old Panchatantra tale, a flock of pigeons, led by their wise king Chitragriva, saw some grains scattered under a tree. They landed to eat, but a hunter had hidden a net there. In a moment, all the pigeons were caught.

Some pigeons began to panic. Each one pulled in a different direction, and the net only grew tighter. Chitragriva said calmly, “If we pull separately, we are weak. Let us all rise together at the same moment.”

The pigeons lifted off together, carrying the whole net into the sky. The hunter ran after them but could not follow. Chitragriva led them to his friend Hiranyaka, a little mouse, who gnawed through the ropes one by one until every pigeon was free.
The pigeons were not strong alone. Their strength came from staying calm, acting together, and having a true friend to help them.
story.moral: Lesson: Real strength comes from unity and good friends, and a calm mind can find a way out of any net.

quiz.q: What is Duryodhana doing in this verse?
o: Naming the brave warriors in the Pandava army
Asking Drona to leave the battlefield
quiz.x: He is pointing out the great heroes standing on the Pandava side.

quiz.q: Which warriors does the verse say are equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle?
o: Mighty archers such as Yuyudhana, Virata and Drupada
quiz.x: The verse names Yuyudhana, Virata and Drupada among the mighty archers and great warriors.

quiz.q: What does the long list of Pandava heroes quietly show?
o: The Pandavas were strong because loyal friends stood with them
quiz.x: Allies like Virata and Drupada were friends and relatives who supported the Pandavas.

quiz.q: What can happen when we only keep counting the strengths of others?
o: Our fear can grow and we may forget our own preparation
quiz.x: Looking honestly is wise, but staring only at others’ strength can feed worry.

reel.hook: Why do we start counting others’ strengths when we feel nervous?
reel.lesson: Know your challenge honestly, but remember your own preparation and your friends.
reel.caption:
Feeling nervous before a big day? 🏹 In Gita 1.4, Duryodhana lists the Pandava heroes one by one.
It is wise to know what you face, but don’t forget your own practice and your good friends.
Take a deep breath and trust your preparation. 🌟
